children: TOKYO, September 17 (Reuters) - Foreign investors turned netsellers of Japanese stocks for the week ending on September 12, capital flows data showed on Thursday.    Foreigners sold a net 1,522.8 billion yen worth of shares inthe week through Sep. 12, after buying a net 689.6 billion yenin the week before that.    Japanese investors bought a net 1,082.9 billion yen of foreignbonds in the latest week after buying a net 111.4 billion yenthe week before.    Details of net investments were as follows (in billion yen):

FOREIGN INVESTMENT IN JAPAN:    (net)                                       stocks         bonds        bills    September 6  - September 12      -1,522.8      +2,236.2     -1,212.8     August 30 - September 5            +689.6r       +444.3r      -275.2
JAPANESE INVESTMENT ABROAD:    (net; a minus sign indicates net selling and inflows of funds into Japan)
stocks         bonds        bills    September 6  - September 12        +169.2      +1,082.9       +150.8     August 30 - September 5            -481.6        +111.4r      +107.1r

Notes:    - An "r" denotes a revised figure.    - Bonds include beneficiary certificates.    - Figures are based on contracts and are rounded.    - The MOF's capital flows data can be found in English at:    http://www.mof.go.jp/international_policy/reference/itn_transactions_in_securities/week.pdf
